analyst_reports.business_description: Fabless designer of PC/server CPUs and discrete GPUs — the #2 player in BOTH markets against dominant incumbents (~80%+ CPU share and ~70-80% discrete-GPU share respectively). Revenue nearly halved over four years as it lost PC share and collapsed to <1% server share (from ~25% a decade ago). The business is kept alive by semi-custom silicon: its chips power BOTH major game consoles under long-term contracts (~$1.6B/yr of stable revenue at scale shown). A respected chip-engineer CEO took over two years ago, cut opex ~30%, refinanced the debt stack, and bet the company on one product.
recent_developments: The company is 12-18 months from launching a CLEAN-SHEET CPU core; management claims ~40% instructions-per-clock uplift vs its current core in internal benchmarks. If real, it would be the first competitive product in a decade. If it slips or underdelivers, the balance sheet leaves little room for another attempt.
Just signed a ~$500M up-front IP-licensing joint venture licensing its server-CPU technology in a large Asian market — non-dilutive cash plus a future royalty stream.
The dominant CPU incumbent's manufacturing lead has visibly slipped — it just delayed its next process-node transition again, the first crack in a decades-long cadence.
Its GPU line is designed into upcoming console refreshes and mid-range VR-capable cards; GPU attach to gaming is growing.
Analyst consensus is deeply skeptical: most sell-side models assume the new CPU core gains little share and value the equity primarily on the console annuity.
analyst_reports.macro_context: PC market shrinking mid-single-digits annually; server demand growing steadily with cloud buildouts; semiconductor cycle bottoming after an inventory correction.
